names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 6 februarie, «Sfântul Cuvios Varsanufie cel Mare».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 6 Φεβρουαρίου, «Όσιοι Βαρσανούφιος και Ιωάννης ο μαθητής του ο επικαλούμενος Προφήτης», with the rank word left off.
Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 6 февраля ст. ст., «Преподобный Варсонофий Великий», with the rank word and the office left off.

death.note: doxologia.ro's life: «A trecut la Domnul pe la anul 540, în chip minunat.» The page says “about the year 540”, not 540; it opens by putting both elders in the sixth century, «în timpul domniei împăratului Iustinian I (483-565)».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 6 февраля ст. ст. — «Прпп. Варсонофия Великого и Иоанна Пророка (VI).»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 6 februarie — «Sfântul Cuvios Varsanufie cel Mare»

attestations.note: The day prints him and John the Prophet as two lines over one and the same life. The site's hymn page for the two of them is a video recording and prints no text but the refrain «Sfinților Cuvioși Varsanufie cel Mare și Ioan Profetul, rugați-vă lui Dumnezeu pentru noi!», so no hymn is recorded here.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 6ης Φεβρουαρίου — «Όσιοι Βαρσανούφιος και Ιωάννης ο μαθητής του ο επικαλούμενος Προφήτης»

Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 19.02.2026 (6. фебруар ст. ст.) — „5. Преподобни Варсонуфије и Јован. Велики подвижници од Газе, прозорљивци и чудотворци. Оставили знамениту књигу Одговора на многа питања о духовном животу. Живели у VI веку.“

attestations.note: Read from the Prologue text on the page, not from its entry list, which dropped this entry whole — the list printed five headings for six numbered entries, and this fifth one was the missing heading. The Prologue keeps the two elders in one entry, as the Romanian calendar keeps them over one life, and gives them four short sentences. It is a second source for the century against the Greek page's: «Живели у VI веку», the sixth, where saint.gr has «Οι Όσιοι Βαρσανούφιος και Ιωάννης έζησαν κατά τον 4ο αιώνα μ.Χ.» and brings in Theodosius the Great. Two sources now read the sixth century and one the fourth; the recorded dates, which are the Romanian page's, are unchanged. The Prologue adds two titles neither other source gives them — прозорљивци, seers, and чудотворци, wonderworkers — and names the place Gaza where the Romanian life has the monastery of Abba Seridos near it.
